parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is a hostile national framework layered with one of the harshest subnational regimes. Universal-exposure exposures are documented at entry (passport marker rules, 'reasonable doubt' refusals, fraud-based lifetime ineligibility, secondary screening), with no effective remedy; neighbouring citizens' detentions confirm these bite visitors. The state adds birth-sex facility rules, licence-marker prohibition, minor name-change denial, care ban, religious refusal licence, and no protections. Severity stops short of the 0.15 tier: imprisonment/execution is not documented for visitors, courts partially enjoin national measures, a bias murder drew a 49-year federal sentence, and majority opinion supports non-discrimination — but state-imposed universal exposure plus state threat-framing keeps this near the 0.35 anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented: national binary passport rules, 'reasonable doubt on sex' refusal cable with fraud-based lifetime bar, passports confiscated abroad, secondary screening outing; foreign advisories issued after detentions of foreign nationals.
entry_documents.protection: Litigation unresolved; FAQ guidance on document strategy.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate to fraud finding and detention; state documents also frozen at birth sex from March 2026.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented national custody harms: forced labour of trans men in immigration custody, beatings, sexual abuse; conversion-style national corrections policies; 24-hour men's-ward holding of an arrested trans woman.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Visa adjudication feeds directly into detention and potential permanent bar.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State public-school facility ban by birth sex; national order bars congruent facility use in funded facilities; 4 state/provinces criminalise certain facility use with one documented arrest (minor).
federal_state_facilities.protection: State trespass offence requires refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; no documented adult arrest in this state.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Hospitals/wards follow document sex, compounding outing.

care_services.exposure: State ban on care under 18; sole adolescent clinic closed; hospital subpoenaed records nationally; religious-refusal statute gives businesses statutory right to refuse; visitors' medication continuity unaddressed.
care_services.protection: National hate-crime prosecution capability exists (49-year sentence, 2017).
care_services.interaction: Emergency care disclosure risks outing; insurance and refusal laws compound.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State court calls trans boy 'minor female'; state in 'legislatively erased' tier; national counterterrorism framing of 'radically pro-transgender' groups; state statute protects refusal based on birth-sex belief.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2024 poll: 67% support statewide GI anti-discrimination law; four municipal ordinances.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises outing severity and police discretionary risk.

minors_guardians.exposure: State supreme court denied trans teen's name change despite parental consent; under-18 care banned; national order directs prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; school dress/sports enforcement with genital/DNA verification clause.
minors_guardians.protection: None documented in state; national litigation pending.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling family faces name/care/school exposures at every institutional touchpoint.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Trans-woman killing rate 6.6/100k vs 6.0 background — near-baseline, not a campaign; 2017 bias murder in this state.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal prosecution achieved 49-year sentence; state hate-crime statute excludes gender identity but national statute covers it.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse functions nationally; local police posture uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: 2025 facility enactment scope, adult enforcement data, licence-law transition terms, dual-listed birth certificate copies. Remedies: injunctions block several national orders but passport restriction was upheld in Nov 2025.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation and municipal ordinances partially mitigate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: No effective remedy for entry refusal; appeals within same agencies rarely succeed.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier: universal visitor-facing document screening with discretionary refusal and no effective remedy, mirrored by the national 'reasonable doubt' cable and documented detentions/strandings. This jurisdiction adds broader societal contestation and functioning courts, slightly above that anchor's closed system.

Materially above: here detention of visitors is occasional and document-driven, not systematic cell-based abuse with impunity; foreign governments issue advisories rather than witnessing routine custodial violence, and a bias killing was punished with 49 years — recourse exists.

Below 0.55-B: that anchor's worst outcome is humiliation and refused entry with functional appeal desks; here the regime adds criminalised facility use in several states, hostile custody documentation, minor-targeted measures, and state threat-framing that 0.55-B lacks.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a national universal-exposure layer — birth-sex passports enforced at entry, screening that outs, a refusal cable with fraud-based permanent bars, and documented abuse in immigration and corrections custody — with a state layer in the harshest tracked tier: birth-sex facility rules, licence-marker prohibition, denial of a trans minor's name change, under-18 care ban, and statutory licence to refuse service. No documented pathway to execution or visitor imprisonment tempers severity, and courts, federal hate-crime prosecution, and majority public support for anti-discrimination law are real mitigations. But the exposures that reach every traveller — documents, screening, facilities, care — are state-enforced with thin working remedy, and foreign visitors have already been detained. That places the jurisdiction at the upper edge of the High Risk band, just above the 0.35 anchors, not into the Reduced Risk tier.
